label: nyiso p11 smoke 2023 (P12 keeper)
definition: NYISO smoke 2023 (P11 structural backcast), re-run under P9b: the measured EIA-930 net interchange is now served by default in load_demand (generalized from PJM-only to {PJM,NYISO,NEISO}). This closes the dominant structural gap the original smoke flagged — NYISO is a ~16%-of-load net importer (−23.45 TWh) and the default path previously served 0, dumping the import wedge on in-state gas. Net-interchange row now GREEN: model −23.45 vs actual −23.45 TWh (duration RMSE 0 MW, import-hours 100%, diurnal corr +1.00). Gas falls 80.11 → 57.52 TWh (+25.6% → −9.8% vs EIA-923 63.79; EIA-930 61.00); TOTAL 147.31 → 123.77 TWh (+16.0% → −2.5%); avg price $70.99 → $42.72. P10 LMP still held (price level-only, not scored). Hydro/nuclear/wind dead-on. No offer band tuned — the interchange gate is green and unblocks the downstream packs (P7 gas+U4 basis, P13 winter oil, P10/U2 LMP, P8/U3 zonal load). PROMOTED TO P12 SIGN-OFF KEEPER (2026-06-12): the P12 loop ran the offer-curve / hydro / storage / import / dual-fuel knobs (probes nyiso 1 gas-actuals, nyiso 2 chp-covered) and found no honest knob improves an in-tolerance class without a zero-sum trade or a convention violation. 2023 mix is calibrated — every renewable/baseload class within ±5% of EIA-923, net interchange exact (RMSE 0 MW); the lone class miss is gas total −9.9% (−5.7% vs EIA-930), a documented EIA-930/EIA-923 demand-basis floor (served total = transmission-metered demand + measured interchange = 123.77 TWh vs EIA-923 129.67), not a dispatch error. oil is U4-gated. 2025/2024 are data-blocked (EIA-930 NYIS stops at Q1'25; preliminary 2025 EIA-923). See docs/calibration-best-so-far-nyiso.md.
